[trixieb] @Big-Deal: Cashback may not track if you use a VPN.
The VPN offers via TopCashback AU that I have posted seem to trade in USD. Some of the VPN companies auto-convert to AUD (estimate) on the website when we access from Australia. The financial institutions seem to view as an international transaction so it's best to pay with a card without international transaction fees.
Regardless of the card used, if using PayPal AU, there could be a currency conversion fee from PayPal AU. I had paid this extra PayPal currency conversion fee with PureVPN and NordVPN although I had used a credit card without international transaction fees. There wasn't an option to convert the currency to USD on the checkout page unlike AliExpress and PayPal AU. Hence I was forced to pay the PayPal currency conversion fees. If you have a USD balance in your PayPal AU account (using Wise), there may not be an extra charge. I'm not familiar with this as I don't have Wise.
There is another currency conversion fee that we have no control of and is written in my tips and TopCashback AU terms. The VPN company seems to report the price charged in USD to TopCashback AU which is converted to AUD in our TopCashback accounts. The currency conversion fee is relative to the price paid and is ineligible for cashback. Hence the reported amount paid in TopCashback AU is usually less than what we actually paid. Cashback is 120% of this reported amount (after deducting the fee) and not what we actually paid.
I only have TopCashback AU. I had asked someone who buys profit PureVPN and other VPN offers via TopCashback US. Cashback is exactly the amount (e.g. 120%) of the price paid in USD in the TopCashback US account as no currency conversion is required.

[jabroni] The company at the centre of this story is Kape Technologies, a London-registered firm wholly owned by Israeli billionaire Teddy Sagi through his investment vehicle Unikmind Holdings. Kape’s portfolio includes ExpressVPN, acquired in 2021 for $936 million; CyberGhost, purchased in 2017; Private Internet Access, bought in 2019 for $127 million; and ZenMate. Together, these services account for three of the six most popular VPN products globally, serving approximately 7.4 million paying subscribers. Kape also owns VPNMentor and Wizcase, review platforms that rank VPN services — including Kape’s own products — for consumers seeking expert guidance.
Before 2018, Kape operated under the name Crossrider. Founded in 2011, Crossrider built a platform used extensively by the ad-injection industry. A 2015 joint study by Google and the University of California identified Crossrider by name among businesses profiting from forced browser advertising. Security firms Malwarebytes and Symantec classified Crossrider-based software as malware. Kape’s CEO, Ido Erlichman, acknowledged the rebranding was necessary due to the company’s association with its “past activities.”
